An issue this package creates never holds a value taken from the input: no token segment, claim value, header value, or key material, and no message from Web Crypto, a schema or a server, since any of those can quote the input. It names which check failed and never what the token said, so a failure can be logged, returned to a client or sent to an error tracker without leaking a token. `path` names claims and header members, which are names this package or your configuration chose, never values. `params.status` of `key_fetch_failed` is the HTTP status code the JWKS server answered with, a number and never content.

Two kinds of issue come from your code, and hold only what it puts in them: an `invalid_claims` path is your schema's path, so a schema over a record can name a payload's own property names there, and a custom key set's failure issues are returned as it gave them. Keep both free of input values if you log them.

Codes and `params.reason` values may gain members in a minor release, when a new check or failure needs its own name; existing ones keep their meaning. Treat an unknown code as a failure like any other, and give a `switch` over codes a `default` branch rather than relying on TypeScript's exhaustiveness check.

There are no messages: a code is the whole answer. Map codes to text yourself if a person needs to read them, and prefer not to tell a client more than "invalid token" when the client may be an attacker.

## Codes

### Token structure

| Code               | Path                                | Params                            | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `malformed`        | none, a segment, or a header member |                                   | Not a string, not three segments, a segment that is empty or not strict base64url, or JSON that is invalid or not an object. Also a non-text `kid`, `typ` or `cty`, and any `b64` header. |
| `too_large`        | none                                | `{ limit: "length", maximum }`    | The token is longer than `maxLength`.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `too_large`        | `["header"]` or `["payload"]`       | `{ limit: "depth", maximum: 32 }` | The JSON nests deeper than 32 levels.                                                                                                                                                     |
| `duplicate_key`    | `["header"]` or `["payload"]`       |                                   | A JSON object repeats a member name, at any depth.                                                                                                                                        |
| `unsupported_alg`  | `["header", "alg"]`                 |                                   | `alg` is missing or not one of the supported algorithms, compared exactly. `none` in any casing is here.                                                                                  |
| `unsupported_crit` | `["header", "crit"]`                |                                   | The header has a `crit` member. No header extension is supported.                                                                                                                         |

### Key selection and signature

| Code               | Path                | Params                                  | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------ | ------------------- | --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `unknown_kid`      | `["header", "kid"]` |                                         | No key in the set has the header's `kid`. A remote set refetches first, outside its cooldown.                                                                                                        |
| `no_matching_key`  | none                |                                         | The header has no `kid`, and no key in the set has its `alg`.                                                                                                                                        |
| `ambiguous_key`    | none                |                                         | More than one key fits the header. Keys are never tried in turn.                                                                                                                                     |
| `alg_mismatch`     | `["header", "alg"]` |                                         | Keys with the header's `kid` exist, but none is bound to its `alg`.                                                                                                                                  |
| `bad_signature`    | none                |                                         | The signature has the wrong length for the key, or does not verify.                                                                                                                                  |
| `key_fetch_failed` | none                | `{ reason }`, and `status` for `status` | A remote key set could not get its JWKS: `reason` is `timeout`, `network`, `status`, `too_large` or `invalid_response`. `key_set_error` means a custom key set threw or returned something unusable. |

### Claims

| Code               | Path                         | Params       | Meaning                                                                                                        |
| ------------------ | ---------------------------- | ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `invalid_claim`    | `["payload", claim]`         |              | A registered claim has the wrong type, such as an `exp` that is not a finite number.                           |
| `expired`          | `["payload", "exp"]`         |              | Now is at or past `exp` plus the clock tolerance.                                                              |
| `not_yet_valid`    | `["payload", "nbf"]`         |              | Now plus the clock tolerance is before `nbf`.                                                                  |
| `issued_in_future` | `["payload", "iat"]`         |              | `iat` is later than now plus the clock tolerance.                                                              |
| `too_old`          | `["payload", "iat"]`         | `{ maxAge }` | More than `maxAge` plus the clock tolerance has passed since `iat`.                                            |
| `wrong_issuer`     | `["payload", "iss"]`         |              | `iss` is none of the accepted issuers, or is not the issuer the selected key is bound to.                      |
| `wrong_audience`   | `["payload", "aud"]`         |              | `aud` contains none of the accepted audiences, or the verifier names no `audience` and the token has an `aud`. |
| `wrong_type`       | `["header", "typ"]`          |              | The `typ` header is missing or is not the required type.                                                       |
| `missing_claim`    | `["payload", claim]`         | `{ claim }`  | A claim required by `requiredClaims`, `issuer`, `audience`, `maxAge` or `requireExpiration` is absent.         |
| `invalid_claims`   | `["payload", ...schemaPath]` |              | Your `claims` schema reported an issue there. The path segments are the schema's.                              |

[Verifying tokens](docs/verifying.md#claim-checks) describes each check.

### Key import

| Code                     | Path                       | Params                                 | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `invalid_key`            | a JWK member, or none      |                                        | The JWK is not an object, a member has the wrong type or encoding, Web Crypto rejected the material, or a PEM string is not one SPKI or PKCS#8 block of a key that fits the algorithm. |
| `unsupported_key`        | a JWK member               | `{ maximum: 8192 }` for an RSA modulus | The key type or curve does not fit the algorithm, the RSA modulus is too long, or the key is multi-prime RSA.                                                                          |
| `weak_key`               | a JWK member, or none      | `{ minimum }`                          | An RSA modulus under 2048 bits, or a secret shorter than its hash: 32, 48 or 64 bytes.                                                                                                 |
| `unexpected_private_key` | a JWK member, or none      |                                        | A public import holds a private member, or is a PEM `PRIVATE KEY` (no path).                                                                                                           |
| `wrong_use`              | `["use"]` or `["key_ops"]` |                                        | `use` is not `sig`, or `key_ops` does not allow the operation the key is imported for.                                                                                                 |
| `alg_mismatch`           | `["alg"]`                  |                                        | The JWK's `alg` names another algorithm than the one you asked for.                                                                                                                    |
| `malformed`              | none, or `["keys"]`        |                                        | From `importKeySet`: the JWKS is not an object (no path), or its `keys` is not an array (`["keys"]`).                                                                                  |
| `too_large`              | none                       | `{ limit: "keys", maximum: 100 }`      | From `importKeySet`: the JWKS lists more than 100 keys.                                                                                                                                |

`importKeySet` and `createRemoteKeySet` skip JWKs that fail these checks instead of reporting them. [Keys](docs/keys.md#importing-a-public-key) describes each check.

## What throws instead

A `TypeError` means a mistake in the calling code, not in the input, and is thrown as early as possible:

- **Options.** Every option of `createVerifier`, `createRemoteKeySet`, `importKeySet`, `readHeader` and the key functions is checked when the function is called, and an invalid one throws, naming the option and its constraint. Every one of them, and `sign`'s input, also throws for a name that is not one of its options, so a typo such as `audiance` cannot silently disable a check or fall back to a default. Create verifiers and key sets at startup and a misconfiguration fails the deploy, not the first request.
- **Key objects.** Passing an object this package did not create where a key is expected, a key of the wrong kind (such as a public key to `sign`), or exporting a key created without `extractable: true`.
- **What you sign.** A payload or header `sign` cannot write exactly as JSON, one that breaks the rules in [Signing tokens](docs/signing.md), or an `embedKey` that is not the public half of the signing key.

A `TypeError` message names the option or member and the rule it broke, never its value.

Three things propagate rather than becoming a result: an exception thrown by your own `claims` schema, a `now` option that returns something other than a finite number, and a failure of Web Crypto itself while signing or generating a key, which means the runtime lacks the algorithm. A verifier's `now` makes its promise reject with a `TypeError`, for a token whose signature checked out. A remote key set's `now` makes its `select` reject with a `TypeError`; a verifier using that key set catches the rejection like any other key-set error and reports `key_fetch_failed` with `{ reason: "key_set_error" }`.

<!-- Source: docs/changelog/0.1.0.md -->

# 0.1.0

0.1.0 is the release `@codenhub/oidc` and the applications built on it are meant to build on. It adds the remaining JWS algorithms, PEM and certificate import, DPoP proofs, JWK thumbprints, `tokenHash` and `importKeyPair`, lets a remote key set answer from stale keys while it refetches, closes what three audits found, and raises the Node.js floor to 26. Each breaking change is marked below with what to do.

## Added

- `ES384`, `ES512`, `RS384`, `RS512`, `PS384`, `PS512`, `HS384` and `HS512`, for generating, importing, signing and verifying. An HMAC secret must be at least as long as its hash: 48 bytes for `HS384` and 64 for `HS512`. The [algorithm table](docs/index.md#keys-are-bound-to-one-algorithm) lists them all. From this release, an algorithm may be added in a minor version, which widens `JwsAlgorithm`, `AsymmetricAlgorithm`, `SymmetricAlgorithm` and the JWK and header types: give a `switch` over an `alg` a default branch.
- PEM import: `importPublicKey` takes a `PUBLIC KEY` block (SPKI), and `importPrivateKey` and `importKeyPair` a `PRIVATE KEY` block (PKCS#8), with a new `kid` option to name the key. Every JWK check runs on the key read. [Keys](docs/keys.md#importing-a-pem-key) covers it.
- `sign({ ..., embedKey })` writes a public key as the `jwk` header, for DPoP proofs (RFC 9449), and `jwkThumbprint(publicKey)` computes the RFC 7638 thumbprint a `cnf.jkt` claim carries. [Signing tokens](docs/signing.md#dpop-proofs) shows a proof signed and verified.
- `createRemoteKeySet` accepts an `http:` URL on `localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8` or `[::1]`, for an identity provider running locally.
- `importKeyPair(privateJwk, { alg, extractable? })`, which loads a signing key stored with `exportPrivateJwk` as `{ privateKey, publicKey }`, like `generateKeyPair`'s result, so the public JWK no longer has to be stored beside it. It proves the two halves belong together by signing and verifying a fixed message, so a JWK whose public members belong to another key is `invalid_key`. [Keys](docs/keys.md#importing-a-key-pair) covers it.
- `importPublicKey` takes a PEM `CERTIFICATE` block and imports the key inside it. Nothing else in the certificate is checked: not its dates, issuer or signature. [Keys](docs/keys.md#importing-a-pem-key) covers it.
- `jwkThumbprint` accepts a private key too, extractable or not, and gives the thumbprint of its public half, so a signer can name its key without keeping the public key around.
- `tokenHash(value, alg)` computes the OpenID Connect `at_hash` and `c_hash` claims for every algorithm the package signs with, `EdDSA` included. [Signing tokens](docs/signing.md#token-hashes-in-id-tokens) shows it.
- `JWS_ALGORITHMS`, `ASYMMETRIC_ALGORITHMS` and `SYMMETRIC_ALGORITHMS`, with the guards `isJwsAlgorithm`, `isAsymmetricAlgorithm` and `isSymmetricAlgorithm`, and `encodeBase64Url` and `decodeBase64Url`, so a caller no longer copies them. [Keys](docs/keys.md#algorithms) lists them.
- An `issuer` option on `createKeySet`, `importKeySet` and `createRemoteKeySet` binds each key to the issuer whose key it is, and a verifier then requires that `iss` for a token the key verifies. Without it, a verifier holding several issuers' keys accepted a token signed with one issuer's key that claimed another's `iss`. Give it to every key set when one verifier serves several tenants; [Key sets](docs/key-sets.md#keys-of-several-issuers) shows how. A key's new `issuer` member says what it is bound to, and `CreateKeySetOptions` is exported.
- `createKeySet` and `importKeySet` return a `LocalKeySet`, whose `keys` lists the set's keys, so an issuer can publish its JWKS from the set it verifies with.
- `createVerifier` options: `allowExpired`, which accepts an expired token whose other checks pass, for an OpenID Connect `id_token_hint`; `audience: false` and `requireExpiration: false`, which waive the new defaults below; and `type` as an array, where `null` accepts a token without `typ`. [Verifying tokens](docs/verifying.md) covers them.
- `createRemoteKeySet` options: `seed`, to start from a JWKS saved earlier instead of fetching on the first token; `onFetch` and `onFetchError`, to save each fetched JWKS and log failures; and `waitUntil`, which on Cloudflare Workers keeps a fetch running after the request that started it has responded. [Key sets](docs/key-sets.md#persisting-the-cache) shows a cache saved between requests.
- `sign` is generic over the payload type, so claims declared as an `interface` compile, while a member that is not a JSON value, such as a `Date`, no longer does. `JwtRegisteredClaims` and `JsonCompatible` are exported for it.
- An [API reference](docs/reference/index.md) generated from the package's TSDoc.

## Changed

- **Breaking.** A verifier without `audience` refuses a token that has an `aud` claim with `wrong_audience`, as RFC 7519 §4.1.3 requires; in 0.0.1 it accepted a token meant for any other service of the same issuer. Set `audience` to your own, or pass `audience: false` to accept any audience on purpose.
- **Breaking.** A token without `exp` is `missing_claim` with `{ claim: "exp" }`, unless `maxAge` is set; in 0.0.1 such a token never expired. Pass `requireExpiration: false` for tokens that carry no `exp` by design.
- **Breaking.** `importPrivateKey` proves a JWK's public members belong to its private key, as `importKeyPair` does, by signing and verifying a fixed message. A JWK mixing two keys is `invalid_key`, and each import costs one signature and one verification.
- When no key in a set has the token's `kid`, the one key without a `kid` that has the token's `alg` is selected, instead of `unknown_kid`. A PEM key has no `kid`, and issuers such as Clerk and Supabase name one in every token, so a set holding just that key refused every token. A remote set refetches its JWKS first, within its cooldown, so a key rotated in under that `kid` is still found.
- Within `maxStale` after `cacheTtl`, a remote key set answers from the expired JWKS at once and refetches in the background; only a `kid` the cache lacks waits for the fetch. A token waits for a running fetch at most until a second past its `timeout`, and, unless the cooldown is running and the cache is still usable, fetches again itself when that fetch misses the deadline or was cancelled with the Cloudflare Workers request that started it; pass `waitUntil` on Workers so the fetch is not cancelled. A key removed from the JWKS stays trusted until the background fetch replaces the cache.
- **Breaking.** `engines.node` is `>=26`, so Yarn 1, and npm with `engine-strict`, refuse the install on Node.js 24 or 25. Upgrade Node.js to 26. Browsers, Deno, Bun and Cloudflare Workers are unaffected. ([#553](https://github.com/codenhub/codenhub/issues/553))
- **Breaking.** Every function that takes options, and `sign`'s input, throws a `TypeError` naming any member it does not know, even one set to `undefined`. In 0.0.1 a typo such as `audiance` was ignored, which turned the audience check off without a sign, and one such as `extractible` silently gave a key that could not be exported. Fix the name the error gives.
- `nbf` and `iat` allow at least 60 seconds of clock skew whatever `clockTolerance` says, so a token checked the moment it is issued no longer fails on a verifier whose clock is slightly behind the issuer's. `exp` and `maxAge` still use `clockTolerance` alone. A token whose `nbf` or `iat` is less than 60 seconds ahead now verifies.
- **Breaking.** `JwsAlgorithm`, `AsymmetricAlgorithm`, `SymmetricAlgorithm` and the key, JWK and header types built on them gain the new algorithms, so code that checks at compile time that it handles every algorithm, such as a `switch` ending in a `never` assignment, fails to compile. Handle the new ones or add a default branch.
- `importKeySet` and `createRemoteKeySet` bind a JWK without `alg` to the new algorithms too, under the default `algorithms`: an `RSA` key also answers to `RS384`, `RS512`, `PS384` and `PS512`, and `P-384` and `P-521` keys are imported instead of skipped. Pass `algorithms` to keep the old set.
- **Breaking.** When `now` returns anything but a finite number, the verifier's promise rejects with a `TypeError`, and so does a remote key set's `select`, which a verifier reports as `key_fetch_failed` with `{ reason: "key_set_error" }`. In 0.0.1, `now: () => NaN` passed expired tokens and kept a remote key set's cache from ever expiring. Return milliseconds, as `Date.now` does.
- **Breaking.** `importSecretKey` takes `Uint8Array | object`, so passing a string is a compile error. At run time a string still returns `invalid_key`. Encode the secret to bytes first, such as with `new TextEncoder().encode(secret)` when it is text.
- **Breaking.** `sign` rejects `-0`, which JSON writes as `0`; an array whose prototype is not `Array.prototype`; and a value with a `toJSON` method anywhere on its prototype chain, a polluted `Object.prototype` or `Array.prototype` included. Each would have signed a different value than the one given. Pass plain data.
- **Breaking.** A custom key set's failure is passed through only when every issue is an object with a string `code` of its own; a list with a hole, or an issue without such a `code`, gives `key_fetch_failed` with `{ reason: "key_set_error" }`, as other key set mistakes already did. Return issues built as `{ code: "unknown_kid" }`.
- **Breaking.** `sign` throws a `TypeError` for an `exp`, `nbf` or `iat` above 253402300799, the last second of year 9999, which is almost always `Date.now()` in milliseconds and signed a token valid for some 55,000 years. Write seconds: `Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)`. Verifiers still accept such values from other issuers.
- `generateKeyPair` retries an `EdDSA` or `Ed25519` generation that Web Crypto rejects with `OperationError`, up to three times. Linux builds of WebKit fail about 1 in 128 such generations at random; drop any retry of your own.
- Issue codes and `params.reason` values may gain members in a minor release, and an existing one never changes meaning. Give a `switch` over codes a default branch.
- `typ` compares ASCII letters without regard to case, and drops a leading `application/` only when no other `/` follows, as RFC 7515 §4.1.9 says. 0.0.1 used `toLowerCase`, which also folded some letters beyond ASCII, such as the Kelvin sign (U+212A) to `k`, and dropped `application/` from values such as `application/a/b`. A `typ` spelled that way no longer matches.

## Fixed

- `exportPrivateJwk` writes an EC or Ed25519 `d` at its full length on WebKit, which drops its leading zero bytes on export. 0.0.1 exported about 1 `ES256` key in 200 in a form `importPrivateKey` then refused as `invalid_key`; an `ES512` key would have failed about half the time.
- Key options are read as own properties, so a polluted `Object.prototype` can no longer make a generated or imported key extractable.
- `importSecretKey` and JWK import accept a `Uint8Array` or a plain object from another realm, as Jest and jsdom give, which 0.0.1 refused as `invalid_key`.
- A remote key set treats a clock that steps back as an expired cache and an ended cooldown, so a removed key stops being trusted at most `cacheTtl` plus `maxStale` after the last successful fetch, as documented.
